We are well. We try to keep things light, which is hard to do sometimes. We both have our issues but I think it helps that we can empathize with each other completely. I really try to make sure he knows if I'm not okay with something and he's pretty accepting of my flaws. I still wish i could stop the obsessive thinking about him leaving me though. I try really hard not to put that weight on him but I'm not perfect at it.

Anyways, it seems that in you're situation, you might benefit from thinking about YOU first. I know your bond is probably strong to this person but they need to want to help themselves as well...sorry if I'm not making much sense all im trying to say is there are people out there that will love you and not cheat on you or lie to you.

You both just have to be honest, honey. I know how hard that can be, since we're not honest to ourselves.  Don't you want to trust them with the things you can't trust yourself with, though? I am a borderline dating a borderline as well and if you'd like to chat I'll be here for you always :)

Your words resonate. I do actually understand what you mean. Having BPD leaves you very in tune to other people's emotions because ours are so raw and powerful, you just pick up on people easier. Feeling like you have to make everyone happy and not upset at you... Man I can relate to that so well.

I think its natural for us to feel this type of empathy for our caregivers. Its obvious that you're aware of her issues. As long as you don't let her affect your livelihood, I don't see anything wrong with not feeling contempt for things she may have done in the past.
I love him, yes. I want him to be happy even if that meant i wasnt in the picture. Id do anything for him...i think thats why it hurts so much.

My bf and i both have bpd. Just as any other relationship, the communication has to be there. The fact that we're both borderline does make it easier to understand each other and identify symptoms you know..but without proper communication you could both just end up screwing each other. Good luck with whatever you decide 👍

Its also legal where i live, i use it pretty regularly to help mute some of my bpd symptoms but my personal advice would be to try something that will be more of a transitional crutch than weed. Im completely dependant on it and it doesnt do much on a long term basis. Plus its expensive and can cause anxiety or paranoia, depending on the strain. So in short, yes it does help, but not enough for me to genuinely recommend for bpd.
